checks: An original active affine plane exists at every source because the current parameter is a finite minimum. Its positivity on the centered source ball gives |c|≤L_*/r_s, independent of any original base slope.

The original plane witnesses feasibility of the constrained base-slope fit. At the minimum-norm fit, an orthogonal component to the span of the active rows can be reduced while preserving all finite inequalities. A fixed independent active row basis gives the least-norm solution to equalities with bounded right-hand sides, and the finite possible bases give a uniform constant, including rank zero.

Each adjusted majorant has the right value at its source. The full mean and L-mean yield equality in its row by integrating the nonnegative gap. The positive mixture is equivalent to sampled d-volume; continuity upgrades equality of the finite minimum to the closed sampled fibers.

Bounded intercepts and slopes give simultaneous coefficientwise subselection and uniform convergence of finite minima on compact sets. Affinity and Hausdorff convergence pass nonnegativity from sampled fibers to their limiting hull.

The weighted sum of log fiber maxima is nonnegative by zero total log integral. Uniform upper maxima and positive volumes force each maximum to stay above a fixed positive level. The segment from a maximizer to the opposite boundary gives the distance lower bound, and the centered inball homothet controls collar volume linearly.

For a point in the current body but outside the limiting t-core, its distance to the current boundary is at most t plus the support-function error. The uniform collar bound on negative logs therefore suffices for convergence of the log normalization, while positive logs are bounded. Limit positivity on each sampled interior follows from the same distance inequality; the finite zero planes then have only boundary faces, of zero d-volume.
